title: Interconnection Network Explorer
description: Click any node in a six-stage supply chain to trace which parts a disruption there would reach, directly and indirectly.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Foundations of Systems Thinking

educational.learningObjective: Given a supply-chain network diagram, the learner will trace which nodes are affected, directly and indirectly, by a disruption at a chosen node.
prerequisites: Knows what a node and an edge are
Has seen a system drawn as a diagram of connected parts
learningOutcomes: Trace the downstream reach of a disruption through a network
Distinguish direct effects from indirect effects
Explain why a node with few direct connections can still have wide reach
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Give learners a node and ask them to list the directly affected nodes and then the indirectly affected ones, without clicking. Check whether they follow the dashed edge as well as the main chain.

pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Prediction before observation, then explanation of the gap
pedagogical.feedbackType: Color highlighting plus a generated sentence naming affected nodes
misconceptionsAddressed: That only directly connected parts are affected by a disruption
That a supply chain is a single linear sequence
discussionQuestions: Why did the 2021 chip shortage surprise car manufacturers who had no direct relationship with chip factories?
If you could add one connection to make this network more resilient, where would you add it?
Does being upstream always mean having more influence?
